items.title: Eikichi Iwai, bassist of Final Fantasy XIV band THE PRIMALS, has died
items.summary: Eikichi Iwai, the bassist of THE PRIMALS, the official rock band of Square Enix's online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV, has died suddenly.
items.content:
Add us on Image credit: Square Enix Eikichi Iwai, the bassist of THE PRIMALS, the official rock band of Square Enix's online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV, has died suddenly.

The news came first from Chirinuruwowaka, another band Iwai played bass in, before THE PRIMALS and the Final Fantasy XIV team confirmed it on X (formerly Twitter) . Neither statement gave a cause of death. The joint message was signed by the members and staff of THE PRIMALS and the Final Fantasy XIV development and operations teams.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock," the statement read. "The members of THE PRIMALS and the entire FFXIV Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow."

In its own announcement , posted in Japanese, Chirinuruwowaka's staff said the members were finding the news hard to accept. The band has cancelled every show of its Doudou Meguri 2026 -Public- tour and apologised to fans who had planned to attend. It said details on ticket refunds will follow.

According to the band's official profile , Final Fantasy XIV Sound Director Masayoshi Soken has led THE PRIMALS since 2014. Its line-up is Soken on guitar and vocals, Michael-Christopher Koji Fox on vocals, GUNN on guitar, Tetsuya Tachibana on drums and Iwai on bass.

The group released its major debut album, THE PRIMALS, in May 2018 and recorded the main theme for the Dawntrail expansion. It sold out a two-day show at Makuhari Messe Event Hall in June 2022 and played two days at Yokohama Arena in September 2024 to mark its tenth anniversary. THE PRIMALS has also played its own shows in Seoul and appeared at Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festivals in North America, Europe, South Korea and China.

The Japan show mentioned in the statement was Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo , where Square Enix showed off the next expansion, Evercold.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Players Mourn The Primals Bassist With In-Game Funerals and Gatherings
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.

Eikichi Iwai was the bass guitarist for The Primals, a band formed specifically to make some of the music in Square Enix’s extremely popular MMORPG. While they aren’t the only ones responsible for some of the game’s iconic tunes, they’re certainly some of the most notable, and they’ve become a firm fixture in the Final Fantasy fanbase over the years.

Iwai’s death was officially announced on November 11, 2026 by his own rock band, Chirinuruwowa, and the Final Fantasy XIV development team, the latter of which penned a public letter to fans informing them of the news.

“As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the statement reads. “Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of THE PRIMALS and the entire FFXIV Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

“As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences.”

Chirinuruwowa published a similar statement on social media. “We regret to inform you that our bassist, Iwaieikichi, has passed away suddenly,” the group wrote. “The sudden news of his passing has left all of us in the band and on the staff struggling to come to terms with it, and we are deeply saddened.” The band also informed fans that all upcoming performances in their Endless Loop 2026 -Public- tour have been cancelled.

Iwai's death sent shockwaves throughout the FFXIV playerbase. In acknowledgement of his legacy as a performer and paying tribute to his contributions to the game, these players gathered together within their respective servers to hold virtual funerals in some of the MMORPG’s fantastical locales.

For example, players on the European server Omega formed a circle around Limsa Lominsa’s Aetheryte Plaza, lighting campfires in remembrance of the bassist. And in the Sephirot, Materia DC server, players hung out for more than seven hours at Ultima Thule, calmly sitting in its field of flowers.

Fans, content creators, and fellow members of the games industry have shared their own fond memories of the game and the impact Iwai's music had on their lives.

@FF_XIV_EN A small memorial for Eikichi Iwai on Omega (Chaos). Thank you for everything, Iwai-san. Your final performance at Tokyo Fan Fest was incredible Chaos DC・オメガでイワイエイキチさんを偲ぶ小さな集まりを開きます。 イワイさん、ありがとう。東京ファンフェスでの最後の演奏最高でした https://t.co/2204TnVxIU

Somehow some people are still here 7 hours later (I've just been doing other stuff) I'll just leave my character here overnight as I'm going to sleep if anyone wants to continue the memorial feel free to come here at Ultima Thule, Sephirot, Materia DC #THEPRIMALS #ffxiv https://t.co/l0YB7Ny45Q

イワイエイキチさん いつも素晴らしいエネルギッシュなLIVEをありがとうございました イフリート鯖のイフリートの祭壇 (X35.2 Y19.8)の追悼の場からお悔やみ申し上げます #FF14 #THEPRIMALS https://t.co/Mi2oJtMiS5

“This one truly hurts… Words just can't describe the shock and grief I'm feeling right now,” YouTuber and game composer Alex Moukala wrote . “FFXIV fans lost an absolute icon. Many bass players around the world lost a hero. And those who knew Eikichi-san personally lost an incredibly kind friend. Rest in peace, Eikichi-san.”

“Eikichi-san was an absolute legend. This is so sudden and devastating. My sincere condolences to his family and friends. May he rest in peace,” another fan said .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Game Band The Primals' Bassist Eikichi Iwai Dies
items.summary: Iwai had just performed concert with MMORPG
items.content:
Iwai had just performed a concert with the band during the game's Fan Festival event in Tokyo on November 1.

The Primals, led by the composer and sound director of Final Fantasy XIV Masayoshi Soken, have performed official cover music from Final Fantasy XIV since 2014. They have released multiple albums for the series and have performed in events, including the game's own official Fan Festivals.

The members include (pictured right from left to right) Michael-Christopher Koji Fox (vocalist and game's localizer, translator, and lyricist), Iwai (bassist), Masayoshi Soken (guitarist, vocalist, and game's composer), Tetsuya Tachibana (drummer), and GUNN (guitarist).

Square Enix released Final Fantasy XIV Online for personal computers in September 2010. Square Enix has since released five expansions: "Heavensward" in June 2015, "Stormblood" in June 2017, "Shadowbringers" in July 2019, "Endwalker" in December 2021, and "Dawntrail" in July 2024. The game's "Evercold" expansion will launch on February 19 for early access, and officially on February 23.

items.title: Eikichi Iwai, Bassist of Final Fantasy XIV Band THE PRIMALS, Has Passed Away
items.summary: Eikichi Iwai, bassist for the FF 14 band THE PRIMALS, has passed away at age 57.
items.content:
Music makes many games what they truly are, setting the tone and doubling down on a moment's emotions, whether somber, pulse-pounding, or chilling. Without their OSTs, many games would feel like a shell of themselves , solid without the soul. Many games have used the need for music to get musicians on the map or back into the public spotlight, creating a beautiful loop.

The EU's proposed Digital Fairness Act targets loot boxes, pay-to-win mechanics, unclear in-game prices, and subscription traps.

Final Fantasy is a series absolutely defined by its music, with truly legendary composers and artists stemming from every title. Sadly, Final Fantasy 14’s Twitter announced earlier today that Eikichi Iwai, bassist for the band made for the game THE PRIMALS, has passed away. After recently performing at the most recent Japanese Fan Fest, his passing is a sudden low blow that has staggered fans across the globe.

THE PRIMALS are the standout musicians of Final Fantasy 14 , far from the only incredibly talented maestros making the music happen, but definitely the flashiest. Often brought out to live events for both their own original tracks and covers of some of 14's other greatest hits, THE PRIMALS helped forge some of the greatest tracks to grace Final Fantasy 14, and Iwai-san's absence will be deeply felt in future events.

While the rest of the musicians behind FF 14 and his bandmates on THE PRIMALS will feel the most potent loss, fans across the globe are aching as well, already holding in-game mourning vigils throughout Eorzea. Sitting by fires and playing different pieces of music Iwai worked on, fans are lamenting his passing the best way they know how, by celebrating all he gave to them.

THE PRIMALS are the standout musicians of Final Fantasy 14, far from the only incredibly talented maestros making the music happen, but definitely the flashiest.

THE PRIMALS have backed some of the most pivotal moments in Final Fantasy 14’s history, bouncing from raid layers to incredibly crucial story moments to general world traversal. As a band, they’re incredibly flexible and talented, with a good part of that grit coming from Iwai’s incredible bass play. The future of the band is currently uncertain, especially with how sudden Iwai’s loss truly was.

Eikichi Iwai passed at age 57, a titan of his craft and an incredible musician across his pursuits, charming millions who played Final Fantasy 14 and all who followed his long history with the band Chirinuruwowaka, of which he was a founding member. Never one to slow down or stop making music, with his recent showing at the latest Japanese FF14 Fan Fest being cited as one of THE PRIMALS best ever showings.

After suffering a loss like Iwai’s, it’s important to remember just how lucky we are to enjoy such incredibly skilled artists in their primes. Final Fantasy 14 has its issues, but music has never been one of them, carrying many crucial emotional scenes with next-level tracks again and again.

Close in the Distance, A Long Fall, and Rise, all written by Masayoshi Soken, show a mastery of tone and emotion across an incredible range, perfectly putting players in the mindset of the current moment. THE PRIMALS’ own coverage of tracks like Footfalls and Dawntrail gives each song life, fueled by THE PRIMALS’ incredible energy.

I genuinely believe you could find someone who cites almost every song in Final Fantasy 14 as one of their favorites, and that’s amazing. The incredible display of artistry throughout the title is a large reason why it has lasted as long as it has with the massive fanbase it has cultivated.

With live service games and MMOs like Final Fantasy 14, it can be all too easy and lucrative to fall into the trappings of consumerism, focusing on the product rather than the art. FF really doesn’t have that issue. FF14 has always felt like a title guided by the artists who create it, and after the loss of such a powerful artist, it’s up to the rest of us to keep on that path. Rest in peace, Eikichi Iwai.

items.title: Fans Gather In Final Fantasy XIV In Memorial For Eikichi Iwai, Bassist For The Primals
items.summary: His passing comes days after he performed at Fan Fest Japan 2026
items.content:
Eikichi Iwai, bassist in the Primals, the official band for Final Fantasy XIV , has passed away. Square Enix and Final Fantasy XIV accounts announced the news of his passing on social media. “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the announcement said . In the wake of Iwai’s passing, memorials are popping up across multiple FFXIV servers as fans remember him and the music he was part of.

In addition to Iwai, the band is led by Final Fantasy FFXIV composer Masayoshi Soken and features musician Gunn on guitar, Tetsuya Tachibana on drums, and Michael-Christopher Koji Fox on vocals. Fans might recognize Koji Fox as being the English localization and translation director for a number of Final Fantasy games.

Much like Nobuo Uematsu’s band the Black Mages, the Primals are known for their rock arrangements and original music for the Final Fanasy XIV soundtrack. W anna hear a rock version of “ Flow “? They got you. You wanna start crying at 10:30 in the morning like I am? “Footfalls” is good for that. I’ll be the first to admit “ To the Edge ” is not one of my favorites out of the Primals’ catalogue (please don’t hurt me), but even I can’t deny Iwai’s sick-ass bass line. His bass makes that song and every one of the Primals’ songs. Iwai’s loss will be profoundly felt.

Square Enix holds Final Fantasy Fan Fests across the world every year featuring a performance by the Primals as one of the main attractions. Iwai’s final performance was at Fan Fest Japan earlier this month, and you can watch a portion of that performance here .

“Going to have The Primals on the whole time I’m playing tonight,” read a comment in the FFXIV subreddit. “Rest easy, Eikichi, thank you for all those basslines.”

items.content:

A post went out on The Lodestone in the early hours of this morning (November 11) which read: "Thank you very much for your continued support of The Primals. As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."

The Primals is Final Fantasy 14's in-house band, fronted by composer Masayoshi Soken and localisation lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and accompanied by Tetsuya Tachibana, GUNN, and Iwai himself.

As Final Fantasy 14's doors remain closed, surviving players are stepping in to keep everyone's crops alive Star Trek Online players are holding public vigils to mourn Patrick Stewart Final Fantasy 14: Evercold delayed to February, preorders start next week FINAL FANTASY XIV: Dark Decades Tour BUDOKAN - Ride the Rhythm Music Video (THE PRIMALS) - YouTube Watch On Iwai's bass in particular has elevated a ton of already-excellent tracks across the game's history: Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze, Shadowbringers' To the Edge, Endwalker's Scream and Close in the Distance, and Dawntrail's Ride the Rhythm just to name a few. The Primals has just come off the back of a strong year for live performances, too—from their usual appearance at all three Fan Festivals that took place this year, to even taking the stage at the UK's biggest rock and music festival as part of Download's lineup .

A quick trip through some of Final Fantasy 14's European servers have seen tons of players gathering in main hubs like Limsa Lominsa to pay their respects and share what it is about Iwai's work that meant so much to them. As I write this story, players and campfires line the perimeter of Omega's Limsa Lominsa plaza—a common practice for honouring the passing of key community figures and beyond, something which I've previously witnessed for the likes of Berserk's creator Kentaro Miura and Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama.

It's a small gesture, but one which is a pleasant reminder of why Final Fantasy 14 continues to maintain such an iron grip on myself and many others.
